title: Drangleic
snippet: As Vendrick went hollow, Drangleic still suffered the onslaught of the Giants; when its army seemed about to be overwhelmed, an unknown warrior felled the Lord of the Giants, whose beaten and broken remains were then dragged beneath a stronghold to be sealed away, leaving the remaining Giant forces to scatter and flee without the resonance of their leader to guide them. In the meantime, the soldiers of Vendrick defending their fortress died and eventually became hollows, though they continued to defend their country with honor, patrolling the area. Even with the Giants eventually defeated, victory had come all too late. Without a king, an exhausted army and with a country reduced to rubble, depopulated and infested with hollows, the kingdom of Drangleic fell apart. The king was seduced by Nashandra's words, and followed her advice to gather an army and cross the Northern Sea, in an effort to subjugate the Giants and claim their souls for himself. title: Drangleic

title: Drangleic
snippet: As the war dragged on, Vendrick's army began a decline caused by attrition in the face of the Giants' will of steel. The king was forced to hire mercenaries from Forossa and Volgen to reinforce his ranks, and Desert Sorceresses from Jugo were added to the defense of the Royal Castle. The endless battles also began to take their toll on the population. Those who could afford it ran away to other countries while the poor were left without a place to sleep, the kingdom now reduced to ruins. The conflict continued for three generations unabated, with the Giants sustaining their attacks on northern fortifications and trying to push their way inland towards the Royal Castle. The bodies of the many dead giants that littered the region slowly grew into great trees, covering the area around Cardinal Tower in a dense forest.

title: Drangleic
snippet: With his army exhausted by losses and desertions, Vendrick was forced to use the arts of the Old Iron King to produce the ancient Ironclad Golems, iron husks that were granted life with an enchantment of souls. These warriors wearing decrepit armor one day emerged from the Drangleic Castle and quietly assumed positions among the royal army, without speaking a word or revealing their faces. At the peak of the war against the Giants, Vendrick abandoned all moral reservations and attempted to revive the terrible experiments that his brother had carried out and which had led to the birth of the Primal Knights. Even if only fragments of the rituals remained, the king restored the forbidden art to create the inhuman abominations, to obtain warriors that would match their enemies in brute strength thanks to immensely heavy shields, swords and armor.

title: Drangleic
snippet:

 drangleic_s_rise : The kingdom of Drangleic was founded by Vendrick when he, together with his older brother Aldia and his mighty army, invaded and trampled the domains of the Old Iron King, the ruins of previous realms, and the surrounding lands, uniting the inhabitants of the region under his banner.

title: Giant Lord
snippet:
Giant Lord -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Giant Lord is the king of all Giants. After his kingdom was invaded by King Vendrick, who was under the influence of Nashandra, the Giant Lord invaded Drangleic to avenge his losses, and to retrieve the prize that Vendrick stole from him. Possessing a will of iron, the giants laid siege to Drangleic in a war that lasted for generations, and laid waste to the once proud kingdom. Eventually the Giant Lord was defeated by an unknown hero, and the giants retreated, crossing the sea to return home. The Giant Lord himself, broken and beaten, was dragged beneath the fort where he fell, and imprisoned there.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Sir Syan, the king's most faithful knight, volunteered to lead the vanguard against the invaders, to give his lord time to mobilize the army; however his forces were slaughtered without honor by the Giants. The sacrifice of Syan and his party gave the royal army enough time to repel the first wave of Giants. On the north coast of Drangleic, the immense fortress of Cardinal Tower was built, which would become the cornerstone of the kingdom's defense. The army blacksmiths began to produce armor characterized by a shape that favored movement and offered great defense, ignoring all ornamentation in favor of suitability for battle. However, even the magnificent Royal Greatswords used by Drangleic knights were terribly inadequate when fighting the mighty Giants. Despite Vendrick supplying his bravest men with the best equipment available, very few managed to return alive, much less victorious. The king even commissioned replicas of Syan's armor and halberd to commemorate their heroism,

title: Drangleic Castle
snippet:
Drangleic Castle -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : Drangleic Castle was the central point and seat of power of Drangleic during the country's height. King Vendrick and his queen, Nashandra, ruled Drangleic.

title: Drangleic
snippet:
Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : The region of Drangleic is geographically defined by natural barriers: to the north stretches a vast coastline while the other three sides are surrounded by mountains.

Far in the north of Drangleic, beyond the great sea, there is an unexplored continent where the race of the giants lives. To the east, Drangleic borders with the kingdom of Mirrah while in the distant east the land of Jugo and the ruins of the kingdom of Forossa are located. To the northeast, Drangleic borders with the frozen ruins of the kingdom of Eleum Loyce. To the west, Drangleic borders with the city of Volgen. To the south, Drangleic borders with the kingdom of Melfia while in the distant south the land of Lanafir is located.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick organized his army under simple ranks like Royal Guards, Knights, Soldiers and Infantry. He valued his royal army greatly, and included in its ranks even mere infantry, equipping each royal soldier with high-quality equipment crafted by the royal blacksmiths and armor with a design inspired by a brave knight from an old legend. The stalwart soldiers of Vendrick did not abandon their posts even as they became hollows, guarding their stations without relent. Distinguished soldiers were rewarded with magical rings that empowered them to carry more equipment, as proof of their meritorious deeds. Velstadt and Raime, two distinguished knights, became the left and right arms of Vendrick. Raime was enticed by the strength of his lord and acknowledged him as a father figure, while Velstadt was lured into Drangleic from a faraway home and devoted himself in life and death to his lord, eventually forgetting why he even came to the realm. Velstadt also became the leader of the elite

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick's influence extended beyond his kingdom's borders, going so far as ordering his chancellor to hire a craftsman from Mirrah who knew how to manufacture the "geisteel" alloy produced in that country, to give his army an edge over his enemies. Chancellor Wellager managed to bring the artisan Llewellyn to Drangleic with the promise of an immense salary, uncovering the secrets of the alloy of Mirrah. Llewellyn became the castle's resident master smith and began working for Vendrick, distinguishing himself for his lack of ostentation and focus on simplicity and sturdiness. Only for a select few including the chancellor, he also forged armor and shields that combined lightness and strength, as well as a long dagger for the king that Vendrick then gifted to his Chancellor.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Left to his own devices after his brother's failure to grant humans the immortality of dragons, Vendrick desperately sought to purge the curse of Undeath that was slowly devouring his kingdom. One of these experiments was conducted on the Milfanito, creatures conceived by Gravelord Nito to keep Undead under control. They resided in the ruins of the Shrine of Amana close to the Drangleic Castle. At least one Milfanito was taken as prisoner inside the castle and she was bound to a magic ring that was capable of making even hollows appear like humans, as the king was fascinated with reclaiming what he feared he would soon lose. At some point Vendrick learned of the monstrous rituals and experiments that his brother carried out in his Keep even on the subjects of his kingdom. Although they had once sought the truth about souls and a mean to free humans from the curse, their means were different and the fervor of their desperate search had eventually withered their familial ties.

title: Drangleic Set
snippet:
Drangleic Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Traditional Drangleic armor. Belonged to Captain Drummond.

Drummond's ancestors have served Drangleic for generations, principally as defenders of the great fort, but Captain Drummond is the last in this proud line.

[Helm] In his day, King Vendrick was fair and just, and expected the same of his liegemen.
This helm was proof of King Vendrick's trust, an honor, until his transfiguration.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Northern Sea
snippet: During his reign, King Vendrick was advised by Queen Nashandra that across the sea there was the looming thretat of the Giants. Vendrick gathered an army and crossed the ocean, defeated the Giants, pillaged their land and took control of their great power, using it to create the golems and further develop his kingdom. However, the giants, angered by the invasion and barbarism of the king of Drangleic, responded by crossing the sea and directly invading the human kingdom with the desire to take revenge on Vendrick, bringing war that consumed Drangleic for centuries with their directed and burning rage..

title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - war_with_drangleic 
 war_with_drangleic : Giants are primarily known through their conflict with King Vendrick and his kingdom. According to legend, a mysterious woman named Nashandra, said to be of unparalleled beauty, came to Vendrick long ago and warned him of a looming threat across the seas, in the land of the Giants. King Vendrick named Nashandra his queen and crossed the ocean with her to combat the Giants. During this conflict, he pillaged the Giant's lands, and stole an unspecified "prize", which he brought back to Drangleic. Using this acquired power, Vendrick created various types of Golems, who in turn built Drangleic Castle.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Centuries after the end of Vendrick's reign, Drangleic would be known in Lothric as "Drang", the land of the legend of the Linking of the Fire. Vendrick's name has been lost to history, who is remembered only as the "Old King of Want", an ancient ruler that was cursed by an all-consuming thirst, making him no king at all in the end. The Dragonriders of his royal guard and their immense strength are also properly remembered. A group of soldiers, who proclaimed themselves descendants of Drangleic and wore the geisteel armor made by the blacksmith of Vendrick's Castle, abandoned the region and became sellswords. Known as Drang Knights, they scattered across the lands and quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive fighting tactics that utilized twinspears and hammers, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Although Drummond and his forces fought valiantly against their foes, the war of attrition had left the armies of Drangleic crippled. They were simply no match for the Giants, fueled by a singular rage against Vendrick and his sins. Despite the captain's fielty to the kingdom, he too believed the king's barbarism to have been misguided, and he saw greater intellect in the actions of his foes, despite their seemingly barbaric appearance and disposition.

While his men were on the brink of defeat, he still wished to topple the leader of the invading Giants no matter the cost, knowing it would surely bring an end to the conflict. It is then that he met with a mysterious hero not from around those parts: the Bearer of the Curse, who had traveled back in time with the Ancient Dragon's gift. Together, they can team up against the Giant Lord and dispell the invading army for good, signaling the end of the generational war, though it came all to late and most of the kingdom was already lost.

title: Drangleic
snippet: From the day the king returned from his incursion into the land of the Giants, a dark shadow had gradually covered his expression, with even his vassals noticing a change in his character. The king of Drangleic became interested in the fate of other rulers of the past who might have found themselves in a situation similar to his and undertook expeditions on the ruins of the Brume Tower, Shulva and Frozen Eleum Loyce, but later decided to leave those lands cursed by several catastrophes, partially withdrawing his forces and sealing their access via magical altars.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: While the Giants invasion was largely stopped, their souls remained powerful. King Vendrick's elder brother, Lord Aldia, kept Giants in his manor and performed experiments on them in an attempt to recreate a dragon. The outcome of Lord Aldia's experiments is unknown, but oddly when the Ancient Dragon roosting at the summit of Aldia's realm was slain, the soul of a Giant was found in its remains. Legend holds that the Giants' resentment of King Vendrick was possibly emboldened in death. This was proven true when the Bearer of the Curse fought the hollowed remains of Vendrick. With the souls of several Giants in the Bearer's possession, Vendrick was significantly weakened and subsequently defeated.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Drangleic

Drangleic prospered and became an influential nation to the point of making Vendrick known as "the one that ruled over the world of man" Having obtained total political dominion over the lands of Drangleic, he left extant religious institutions and their traditions intact. The king had a lukewarm opinion of their holy powers, and clerics were kept at a distance from the royal court, their inherited roles relegated to ceremonial positions, without opportunities for attaining greater power.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick was the leader of a people of skilled warriors whose cavalry did not employ ordinary horses but instead rode wyrms, a race of land wyverns. Those who fought on the backs of these creatures held the title of Dragonriders, a rank obtained only by their strongest. As a frontline commander, Vendrick favored simple, honest warriors who relied only on their own brute strength; as such, his army avoided dependence on sorceries or miracles, valuing physical ability alone. Before they could aspire to ride wyrms, Vendrick's warriors had to learn to wield great bows that required inhuman strength just to merely draw and great skill to shoot. To become fully-fledged Dragonriders, these knights were then called to tame their wyrms; those who failed to handle the beasts were torn apart and devoured. Those who emerged victorious boasted unmatched strength, and the sight of magic imbued halberd-wielding Dragonriders on wyrm-back soon became a feared sight on the battlefield. Dragonrider

title: Drangleic

At a certain point Raime and Velstadt clashed and Raime was defeated and deemed a traitor, leading him to resign from his post and reconsider his way of life. Reborn as a stalwart warrior, he started to seek someone to whom he could dedicate his life. Velstadt continued to serve at Vendrick's side, as if he was his lord's own shadow.

To make things worse, Vendrick also found himself dealing with the fate of all kingdoms in the history of the region: the First Flame began to weaken, and the number of undead grew. The king himself was forced to draw from the power of his immense soul to keep the curse at bay, feeling it growing despite the strength he had pillaged from the Giants.

title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: Thus passed the centuries and, in the days of Drangleic, not one even remembered the very name of the Ivory King. Although Eleum Loyce remained isolated from the rest of Drangleic due to its forbidding climate and the desolation that surrounded it, a magical shrine remained in the Shaded Woods near the Drangleic Castle who was able to connect the two kingdoms via a portal, access to the city permitted through a magical stone ornament kept by King Vendrick in his castle.

title: Drangleic
snippet: The artisans and blacksmiths of Vendrick studied the advanced metallurgical technologies of the fallen civilization of Heide, to try and replicate the composition of their mysterious alloy. Even though they failed, their attempt to imitate it resulted in a similar bradden steel. This fine alloy was forged from ores that were mined in the south of the kingdom and were widely used, particularly to craft armors that provides a sturdy defense with the design of the ancient elite knights of Astora. The king was also interested in sorcery, coming into possession of magic from Melfia like the Soul Greatsword and rediscovering ancient sorceries from Olaphis like Soul Bolt. Vendrick was also concerned with the history of the kingdoms before his own, collecting different types of Golems created by different civilizations throughout the history of Drangleic like the Old Knights of Heide, the Ruin Sentinels from Olaphis, the Belfry Gargoyles from Venn, the Manikins from Earthen Peak and the Old

title: Drangleic
snippet: Studying and experimenting on the inhuman creatures and their souls, and via studies on artifacts from older kingdoms, Vendrick and Aldia pioneered the creation of Golems, very similar in appearance to the captured giants. Vendrick made Nashandra his queen, and had the golems build his Royal Castle, as proof of his gratitude and affection to her. Beneath the royal castle was the ancient Throne of Want, an artifact capable of connecting to the First Flame, the source of souls and beginning of all that the king was seeking. Studying the First Flame and the mysteries of the soul with his brother Aldia, the king acquired a profound understanding of the history of the world and the rules of reality, how the Flame brought Disparity and everything from it, propagating souls in the world every time someone linked it, giving it new strength. He also understood how the Dark was kept under control as long as the fire flourished, and that once the fire naturally weakened the curse would strike

title: Drangleic
snippet: In the darkest hour of his reign, Vendrick also realized that his Queen, Nashandra, was a creature of the Abyss, and harbored an insatiable desire for strength. She was a fragment of a dark creature taken a human form, obsessed with the King's powerful soul. Impelled by her cravings, Nashandra sought souls, and strove to make the strength of the Giants her own, everything to reach the Throne of Want and the link for the First Flame so it could spread the Dark. Her painting in the castle was in fact able to curse the undead, making them hollow and draining their life, and only the king knew whether the depiction of the Queen was a resentful mockery, or an affectionate exaltation. At this point Vendrick had achieved a profound understanding of the truths of the world. He understood how the fire of souls was not enough to harness the curse, and how the Flame would soon fade and the souls of ancient beings would reemerge, before Dark would descend as a curse on humans, making them take

title: Mirrah
snippet: Towards the end of his reign, Vendrick hired some of the deserting Shadow Knights from Mirrah to fight against the hollows in an attempt to stave off the curse that was plaguing his kingdom. He put them to work in the No-man's Wharf where they sent the imprisoned undead to die in the sea, but before long they became hollow themselves.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Timeline -  Dark Souls III - storyline - the_war_against_the_dragons 
 the_war_against_the_dragons : (**INCOMPLETE**)

The Lords and their armies wage war on the Dragons for control over the surface of the world.
The war against the dragons is very bloody initially, as for every dragon slain three of Gwyn's soldiers perished
The Witch of Izalith and her witches weaved great firestorms, destroying the Archtrees and burning the dragons
Gwyn's eldest son takes part in the war against the Dragons with his father, killing several with his Great Lightning Spear
Gwynevere bless and support her father's knights with her miracles
Pygmies and humans, forced by the gods, take part in the war against the Dragons as Ringed Knights alongside Gwyn's Silver Knights. Their contribution to history, however, will never be recognized.

title: Lindelt
snippet: Thanks to their well-honed miracles and unwavering faith in the face of death, the cleric knights of the Archdrake Church were a formidable force on the battlefield, even managing to stand up to the army of King Vendrick as worthy rivals. Miracles like Replenishment and Resplendent Life allowed the knights to endure and heal from arduous battles. Among the high-ranked clerics, Forsalle stood out thanks to his mastery of miracles, and led many battles across his country's borders. He earned the title of "holy knight" and was feared for his "demonic power" by his enemies. However, some cleric knights of Lindelt defected to escape their country's authoritarian rule. These clerics tried to start new lives in the destroyed kingdom of Drangleic and found their way inside the Shrine of Amana, where some of them went hollow.

title: Black Dragon Kalameet
snippet: Regardless, the Dragon Knights, who wore armor forged from the scales of Kalameet and used weapons created from his tail, persisted, and at some point arrived in Drangleic and settled in the Dragon Shrine. The group of knights would also join the covenant of the Dragon Remnants, apostles who venerated the primordial creatures and desired the perpetuity of their existence, seeking their scales to rise above their limited human existence. This group used the Dragon Eyes to invade the space and time of other knights and challenged them to claim their dragon scales, rewarding the best among them with the stones infused with the powers of the dragons to try to achieve transformation, as well as with the ancient Black Dragon Greatsword forged from Kalameet's tail.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Once his army had been prepared and armed with spears and greatbows that used arrows as big as iron spears, Gwyn went to the surface with the intention of waging war against the Dragons and conquering the world with his Lord allies. The war turned out to be very bloody; for each of the majestic creatures slain, three scores of Gwyn's soldiers perished. The bodies of dragons were harder than stone, and resistant to fire and magic, making their killing difficult. At one point Gwyn was even forced to integrate into his ranks the primordial humans, descendants of the Furtive Pygmy who had found the Dark Soul, and who had developed their own weapons and armor infused with the life-giving power of the Abyss.

With their combined might, the four Lords eventually defeated the dragons, beginning a new age.

title: King's Leggings
snippet:
King's Leggings -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Leggings of Vendrick, King of Drangleic.

What makes a king? Some say that it is birthright, while others call it destiny.

Perhaps it is not important, as long as the king's name serves to unite his people.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Royal Guard
snippet:
Royal Guard -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lore 
 lore : High ranking soldiers in Vendrick's army, these knights were gifted weapons and equipment modeled on Sir Syan, one of Drangleic's military leaders. However Sir Syan was killed during the war against the Giants and his armor became cursed. Shortly after his death, the unfortunate knights that wore his armor were driven insane.

title: Dark Souls II
snippet:
Dark Souls II -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - plot 
 plot : The story of *Dark Souls II* is not directly connected to *Dark Souls*, though they are set in the same world.

The game takes place in Drangleic, a once prosperous land under the rule of King Vendrick, which has fallen to ruin throughout the ages with the raging war between humans and giants, the sudden disappearance of the King, and the spreading of the Undead Curse. Like many others, the protagonist has come to the crumbling kingdom in search of a cure for their crippling affliction, the Curse of the Undead.

title: Chancellor Wellager
snippet:
Chancellor Wellager -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Chancellor Wellager was one of Vendrick's most important servants, having been present for all of his greatest accomplishments; the founding of the kingdom of Drangleic, the arrival of his queen Nashandra, the construction of the castle and the invasion of the land of Giants, which resulted in the creation of the Golems. This led to a period of peace that the advisor described to be akin to the Dark, a hint to the queen's true nature.

His king had once ordered him to enlist the great blacksmith Llewellyn from the land of Mirrah with a lifetime contract, so that the kingdom of Drangleic could have access of the rare geisteel from the eastern land, which had been secret until then. Wellager would succeed in this, even being gifted the Espada Ropera by the blacksmith. His exploits would strengthen the kingdom greatly.

title: Dragonrider Greatshield
snippet:
Dragonrider Greatshield -  Dark Souls II - shield - description 
 description : Greatshield of the Dragonriders, King Vendrick's royal guard.

The rank of Dragonrider was reserved for honorable warriors who helped found Drangleic. Together with the King, they crushed its former inhabitants and erected a magnificent kingdom upon their graves.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Once the Ashen Mist Heart has been obtained, it can be used to interact with the corpses of three fallen Giants who fought in the war against Vendrick. The heart grants access to the memories of Jeigh, Orro and Vammar. In these memories, the player can witness various battles that took place between the Giants and Vendrick's army. According to Sweet Shalquoir, the Giants savour their memories of glory on the battlefield.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : Forossa is a land located to the distant east of Drangleic.

The kingdom of Forossa was defined by war, constantly in conflict with its neighbors. Leading up to the fall of the nation, it was engaged in a protracted war with its neighbors. The culture and organization of the Forossan army rightly recognized and rewarded their soldiers for their strength, determination and diligence on the battlefield; those who distinguished themselves could, in the course of their lives, ascend from mere peasants to generals.

title: High Lord Wolnir
snippet: The warriors of Carthus swore their lives to Wolnir, growing ever ruthless and bloody in his name. Under Wolnir's rule, the kingdom of Carthus grew aggressive and expansionist, to the point where it was likened to uncontrollable fire, its beacons being used as war signals. His conquests were spearheaded by his warriors with superior combat skills and combat pyromancies. Wolnir soon subjugated the kingdoms around Carthus, melding the various "crowns" that ruled different lands into a single one, thus ascending to "High Lord". At some point Wolnir stripped three armlets and a holy sword from the corpses of some clerics, demonstrating how religion and gods counted for nothing in his kingdom.

title: Sir Syan
snippet:
Sir Syan -  Dark Souls II - character - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Sir Syan was widely known as the kingdom's most loyal knight, and was King Vendrick's very own retainer. When the giants invaded Drangleic, he volunteered to lead the advance party against them, but was slaughtered most dishonorably. He would never get to behold the greatshield that the king had commissioned for him, named after his glory and meant to immortalize it.

After Syan's death, Vendrick commisioned replicas of his knight's suit of armor as well as his iconic halberd. This equipment would be given to promising knights among his army, to honor his trusted retainer's memory. However, those who had the honor of donning this armor soon lost their mind, with no explanation.

Perhaps it was the burden of living up to Syan's example, or maybe it was his own spirit haunting the suits of armor. The truth of the matter remains shrouded in mystery.

title: Carthus of the Sands
snippet: At some point, the giant humanoid Wolnir rose to power in Carthus. The warriors of Carthus swore their lives to Wolnir, growing ever ruthless and bloody in his name. Under Wolnir's rule, the kingdom of Carthus grew aggressive and expansionist, to the point where it was likened to uncontrollable fire, its beacons being used as war signals. His conquests were spearheaded by his warriors with superior combat skills and combat pyromancies. Wolnir soon subjugated the kingdoms around Carthus, melding the various "crowns" that ruled different lands into a single one, thus ascending to "High Lord". Along the way, Wolnir stripped three armlets and a holy sword from the corpses of some clerics, demonstrating how religion and gods counted for nothing in his kingdom.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa -  Dark Souls III - location - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : In the region and times of Lothric, Forossa was recognized as a kingdom that had been destroyed, but legends about its Lion Knights and those among them that became part of history remained alive.

Following the collapse of Forossa, its survivors, along with other groups originating from Drangleic, contributed to founding the kingdom of Lothric. One of the armor sets that were named for the ancient god of war worshipped by the Forossans was preserved; among the royal guard of Lothric is Lion Knight Albert, descendant of the order of Forossa Knights.

The brigands who survived the fall of Forossa, though no longer identified by their homeland, still roam the world wielding their ancient war axes.

title: Olaphis
snippet:
Olaphis -  Dark Souls II - location - lore 
 lore : Olaphis was a kingdom that once stood on the land which corresponds to the domains of Drangleic under the reign of King Vendrick. The country was one of many kingdoms that rose and fell throughout the history of the region. The immense fortress of the Bastille was the residence of the country's ruler and the nucleus of the kingdom, its land extending as far as the regions that would be later known as Brightstone Cove Tseldora and the Shrine of Amana.

Olaphis was a sophisticated society home to advanced technology and magic, developed in both sorceries and pyromancies. Its craftsmen were credited with complex designs, known for their refined halberds and powerful staves. The kingdom seems to have mined the brightstone in their territories and turned them into crystals, which were used in their catalysts to amplify sorceries.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The old knights of Lothric also turned to the Firstborn of Lord Gwyn for aid, once venerated as a god of war and the sun, who in turn gave them the tools to face the wyverns. From the sun god they would learn how to infuse their weapons with the power of lightning, lethal against dragons, and the ancient techniques for hunting archdragons developed in the war between the gods and the Everlasting Dragons. They also learned of his miracles on manipulating lightning as a weapon.

title: Syan's Helm
snippet:
Syan's Helm -  Dark Souls II - armor - description 
 description : Replica of the helmet of the loyal knight Syan. his solidly-crafted helm offers high defense.

Sir Syan was widely known as the kingdom's most loyal knight, and when the Giants invaded, he volunteered to lead the advance party, but was slaughtered most dishonorably.

The King commissioned replicas of Syan's accoutrements and bestowed them to promising knights, but not long after they donned the armor did they go thoroughly mad.

title: Forossa
snippet:
Forossa was also the origin of the special and powerful black firebombs capable of causing large flames and explosions. These bombs, due to the risk they posed to their owners, were subject to strict standards for their safe storage, codified in the kingdom's legislature.

Forossa eventually fell to war, its military and government exhausted to the point of collapse. The fall of the country left its citizens to their own devices, most of whom became bandits and thieves that infested the outskirts of their fallen home, or scattered across the continent. Without an element of cohesion, the remaining Forossan knights became mercenaries, selling their fighting strength to foreign armies. Among these Lion Knight mercenaries was Vengarl of Forossa, once a ferocious warrior on the battlefield, who came to Drangleic and served under the command of King Vendrick.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet:
Captain Drummond -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Captain Drummond descends from a family line of high-ranking army captains of Vendrick, entrusted with his seaside fort. The helm in their possession is proof of the king's great trust.

However, a long time after the king had subdued the Giants and stolen their prized possession in his conquest, the beings would cross the sea to enact their vengance in a war that continued for generations. The fort overseen by Drummond's family was the main stage of the long-winded massacre, with his grandfather and father both having to face the threat of the Giants, until the duty would be passed down to him, as well as their equipment.

title: Bone Scythe
snippet:
Bone Scythe -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Scythe forged from the soul of the Covetous Demon.

The curved spine of the Covetous Demon is as hard as rock, and rather than slicing through flesh, this weapon seems to grind it apart.

That thing that ended up a monstrous fiend, what was it to begin with, and why did it never leave the queen? Perhaps it was entranced by some perversion of love.

title: Mirrah
snippet: The excellent alloy called "geisteel" had also been invented in the country of Mirrah, and never sold abroad. The rare material allowed the crafting of equipment that offered top-notch protection at a very light weight. As such, its method of manufacture was kept secret from foreign lands, since it provided the kingdom's army with an innovative edge over its enemies. The secrets of geisteel were exported when King Vendrick ordered Chancellor Wellager to hire a craftsman of geisteel. Wellager managed to bring the craftsman Llewellyn back to Drangleic with him. Allocated a blinding salary, Llewellyn became the castle's resident master smith and began working for Vendrick, forging geisteel armor along with long daggers and shields, and distinguished himself for his lack of ostentation and focus on simplicity and strength. His smithy supplied only a select few, including the chancellor himself and the Stone Soldiers and Stone Knights.

title: New Londo Ruins
snippet: The knowledge of the ancient healing sorceries of New Londo somehow survived and reached Drangleic where they were employed this time through miracles like Caressing Prayer, a text developed only around the kingdom of Vendrick and whose authenticity as a sacred text was even questioned, that was able to purify the body and remove all poison of the caster and those close to them.

title: Melfia
snippet: Once an aspiring magician, Felkin the Outcast claims whilst in Drangleic that he studied both sorceries and pyromancy at "a great school in the South"; although he never names the school nor the land, it was likely Melfia, which is south of Drangleic. His wares as a merchant imply that he also studied miracles, as he sells the Magic Barrier miracle as well as items from Lindelt, a land known for its miracles (and where sorcery was anathema), such as the Archdrake Chime used as a catalyst for miracles. Although magically gifted, Felkin did not feel any affinity with either sorcery or pyromancy, but would eventually find his calling in hexes, derived from the very first dark sorceries born during the fall of the long-lost land of Oolacile to Abyss, eventually leading him to come to Drangleic, "where Dark runs deeper than anywhere else", even though, unlike almost everyone else within the fallen kingdom, he is not Undead.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Having accumulated immense knowledge through his vast, twisted experiments, Aldia directed his research towards infusing the qualities of the everlasting dragons into humans, to free them from the shackles of their fleeting form and transcend, like the followers of the Dragon Remnants were trying to do using stones infused with the power of the dragons. The scholar obtained some of the Giants that his brother had captured and kept them in his manor as experimental subjects in an attempt to use their bodies and souls to recreate a dragon, only producing creatures with bones resembling draconic features that were killed once they had outlived their usefulness. His sustained efforts resulted in humans that turned into half-dragons, transformed into undead aberrations with deformed skulls that became close to those of the dragons but still degraded into hollows.

title: Drangleic
snippet: they had once sought the truth about souls and a mean to free humans from the curse, their means were different and the fervor of their desperate search had eventually withered their familial ties. Understanding how his older brother had now abandoned morality to experiment on humans, Vendrick decided to confine him and his servants in his mansion, leaving him alive but building a King's Gate that would limit anyone from entering or leaving that wasn't the king himself, but consequently also losing access to the wyverns raised in the Dragon Aerie beyond the villa that represented an important military asset.
